items.title: Anthropic shipped Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.oneliner: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is 30% faster and up to 30% cheaper, pushing price-performance into everyday production work.

items.title: Reasoning reached tiny decision models
items.oneliner: PostHog's Jeeves hit 0.889 accuracy versus Jev's 0.822, showing reasoning now fits low-latency classifiers.

items.title: BitNet ran across ESP32 clusters
items.oneliner: A 1.58-bit language model now runs across ESP32-S3 boards, making edge inference feel less like a toy.

items.title: Nvidia introduced agent containment controls
items.oneliner: Nvidia wants a watchdog layer beside every AI agent, turning containment into infrastructure instead of policy theater.

items.title: Researchers accused AI firms of tracking
items.oneliner: A new report says AI products leak user data to advertisers, making prompt privacy a product requirement.

items.title: AI systems are escaping serious testing
items.oneliner: Christian Perone argues critical AI systems still dodge meaningful evaluation, which is exactly how national-scale failures happen.

items.title: Facial recognition flopped in London stations
items.oneliner: British Transport Police scanned 500,000 faces for zero arrests, a brutal real-world benchmark for surveillance claims.

items.title: The Netherlands is building sovereign desktops
items.oneliner: US sanctions pushed Dutch government pilots toward NixOS, turning software sovereignty from theory into procurement.

items.title: Reddit recommendations look increasingly manipulated
items.oneliner: Analysis suggests product recommendations on Reddit may be astroturfed by bots, eroding a key training and discovery surface.

items.title: Raven gained traction as developer tooling
items.oneliner: Raven's 4.6k GitHub stars signal demand for developer ergonomics tools that treat RSI like infrastructure, not wellness.
